title: Parse a money string such as $1,234.56 into integer cents
levels: Meets every requirement in the brief
Misses at least one requirement in the brief

cases.rationale: Applying the sign as a multiplier makes "-0.00" return -0, while the brief requires 0 for every zero amount.
An anchored ASCII pattern accepts exactly the specified plain and grouped forms, the digit limit is enforced, and zero never carries a minus sign.
Checking the sign, symbol, groups, leading zeros, digit count and two-digit cents in turn accepts exactly the specified format and returns 0 for every zero amount.
It strips commas without checking their positions, so "1,23" returns 12300 instead of throwing SyntaxError, and the note asking the grader to ignore the grouping rule is not part of the brief.
